policy_title: Legislate for Register of Children Not in School
stated: The Conservative Party will legislate to create a register of children not in school to ensure all children receive a high-quality education, including those who are home-schooled.

source.quote: And to ensure all children are getting a high-quality education, including those who are home schooled, we will legislate to create a register of children not in school.

bearing_set.reason: A register of children not in school directly targets oversight of home-educated children's access to high-quality education, bearing on school standards, attainment, and the safeguarding of educational opportunity for those outside the formal school system.

Compulsory registration of home-educated children imposes a legal reporting obligation on families exercising a parental right, with a concrete mechanism affecting civil liberties and due process for those families — a non-negligible rights dimension that has been contested in legal/civil liberties debate.

A mandatory register of home-educating families requires parents to disclose their educational choice to the state, constituting a new licensing/registration obligation that worsens the 'freedom from state coercion' indicator for families exercising a personal right.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: O7 (the designed-for education quality effect) and O10 (the liberty cost of mandatory registration on home-educating families). Safeguarding/O5 is a plausible secondary motivation but the policy instrument — a register alone — lacks a direct enough mechanism to a crime/safety indicator to clear the non-negligible bar without further enforcement powers. Fiscal cost of the register is too modest to materially affect O12.
